item.title: Shiro-ebi: Toyama Bay's Delicate White Shrimp — Guide
item.description: Shiro-ebi, or white shrimp, are small, translucent shrimp caught almost exclusively in the deep waters of Toyama Bay, one of very few fishing grounds in the world where they occur in commercially viable numbers, earning them the nickname ‘jewel of Toyama Bay’. Prized for their sweet, delicate flavour and slightly firm texture, shiro-ebi are most commonly served raw as sushi or sashimi, though lightly fried tempura and dried kakiage fritters are also popular preparations found throughout Toyama’s restaurants and markets.
